transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-07-15
Time: 16:00 PT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Lara Chen (Redwood AE), Miguel Ortiz (Redwood SE), Sophie Patel (Nimbus Eng Manager), Rajesh Kumar (SRE), Maya Green (CISO)

Summary: quick console walkthrough focused on tracing, request logs, and error analysis flows; security questions around audit logs, KMS, SSO; agreed to run a short benchmark and exchange security docs.

00:00 Lara Chen: alright everyone, thanks for joining, i'll kick us off. i'm lara from redwood, and miguel's our solutions engineer, he'll show the console tracing.
00:12 Sophie Patel: thanks, yep, excited to see how you guys do error analysis, we've been troubleshooting intermittent 503s in prod.
00:18 Miguel Ortiz: cool. so i'll share my screen, let me know if the view is blocked. this is the red-wood console home, apologies if the transcription calls it red wood, it's Redwood Console.
00:35 Miguel Ortiz: first thing i want to show is the request logs page, so you can filter by route, model version, and time window. you can also surface the KV cache hit rates and batching stats in-line.
00:48 Rajesh Kumar: can you filter by customer tenant id? we have multi-tenant traffic and need tenant-level traces.
00:55 Miguel Ortiz: yes, you can; there's a tenant_id field in the request metadata. we also have a mapping to your internal id if you provide the mapping. occasionally the auto-transcript shows it as k v cash, like K-V cash, but it's KV cache.
01:10 Sophie Patel: when you say trace, is this distributed trace across app + redwood runtime or just the request logs?
01:18 Miguel Ortiz: good question — we ingest request-level traces from the runtime and emit OpenTelemetry spans. you can link those spans to your app traces via trace_id. so in the console you can click into a request and then see a waterfall of spans, latency per stage (tokenization, kernel exec, network).
01:34 Miguel Ortiz: example here, this request had a high tail latency at the 'kernel selection' step. you can expand to see exact timings, and download the full span JSON.
01:45 Maya Green: how long do you retain these logs and are they encrypted at rest?
01:52 Lara Chen: retention depends on plan; hosted default is 30 days, Dedicated has configurable retention and can ship to your log storage. everything is encrypted at rest with AES, and for Dedicated/Private we support customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM.
02:09 Maya Green: and for audit logs and compliance evidence?
02:12 Lara Chen: we have an audit log view in the console and an exports endpoint. we also have SOC2 reports and ISO artifacts in the security packet we'll send.
02:20 Miguel Ortiz: jumping back into the trace view — notice the error analysis tab. this one aggregates request failures by error class, model variant, and input signature. you can group by prompt hash to see recurring failure modes.
02:39 Sophie Patel: can you show an example of a flaky 5xx and how you'd debug it?
02:44 Miguel Ortiz: sure. here's a recent 503 cluster: you can see a spike in queue time before the kernel selection. that often indicates contention on the GPU pool or a batching configuration mismatch. the console suggests potential mitigations — e.g., increase reserved batch size or enable adaptive batching for that route.
03:05 Rajesh Kumar: would that be automatic or do we have to change our config?
03:09 Miguel Ortiz: we have suggestions and an 'apply recommendation' button in Dedicated. for Hosted you'd request config change via support or use the API. recommendations include targeted autoscale and route-level cache warmers.
03:22 Sophie Patel: what about correlating user-facing errors with prompt contents? we need to know if specific customer inputs trigger safety filters or model failures.
03:30 Miguel Ortiz: the console flags prompts that hit safety or timeout. you can redact sensitive content in logs on ingest; we also provide a hash-only mode so you get prompt fingerprints without storing full text.
03:44 Maya Green: how about SSO and RBAC? we need SAML and SCIM provisioning.
03:49 Lara Chen: yes, SAML SSO and SCIM are supported; RBAC is role-based with fine-grained route and model permissions. we'll include the SSO setup doc in the follow-up.
03:59 Sophie Patel: any rate limiting visibility? we saw some 429s and couldn't tell if they were client-side or redwood throttling.
04:07 Miguel Ortiz: request logs include response codes and throttle reason. you can filter by 429 and see if it's quota-based, burst, or per-route flow control. we also surface per-token cost and latency so you can debug cost spikes.
04:22 Sophie Patel: can you demo the waterfall for an end-to-end request?
04:26 Miguel Ortiz: yeah, opening a single request — here's the trace id. you can see the initial auth handshake, then network to our edge, scheduling into GPU, kv cache lookup, model forward pass, and return. the p99 here is high due to model forward pass — which correlates to a large sequence length.
04:45 Rajesh Kumar: sequence length, interesting; can Redwood automatically pick a quantized variant for long sequences?
04:50 Miguel Ortiz: we have model variants and automatic fallbacks you can configure in routing policies. the console also recommends quantization profiles for specific workloads.
05:01 Miguel Ortiz: one more thing — error grouping: it clusters similar stack traces and includes sample inputs (if not redacted) and a suggested owner label. you can create a ticket directly to JIRA from the group.
05:16 Sophie Patel: that's useful. can the console annotate anomalies over time? e.g., if 5xx increases after a deploy?
05:23 Miguel Ortiz: yes, we have change-point detection and deployment tagging. you can annotate a rollout and the system will correlate metrics and traces across the window.
05:33 Maya Green: on the security side, what about data residency? some PHI must stay in region.
05:39 Lara Chen: for Private deployments we can deploy the control plane and runtime in your VPC/region; Dedicated allows region pinning. we'll send the chart of region options.
05:48 Sophie Patel: quick perf question — for our throughput target we need sustained 1k req/s with p95 < 400ms for short prompts. can you support that on Dedicated?
05:59 Miguel Ortiz: yes, typically with pooling and autoscale; we'll run a benchmark with your payload. proposal: we provision a Dedicated pool and run 30-minute load test to validate p95 and p99.
06:12 Lara Chen: next steps recap: we'll send security packet (SOC2, SSO/SCIM guide, KMS docs), miguel will run a bench and share methodology, and we'll get sample traffic + hold a tech benchmark next week.
06:25 Sophie Patel: sounds good. one last question — do you have an API to pull raw traces programmatically?
06:30 Miguel Ortiz: yes, the request logs API lets you stream JSON of spans; for large exports we can S3-ship or push to your syslog.
06:40 Rajesh Kumar: great. any blockers on our side to start the benchmark? we'll need an api key and test dataset.
06:45 Lara Chen: we'll issue a scoped API key and a sandbox tenant for the test.
06:52 Maya Green: and you'll provide encryption options for logs?
06:55 Lara Chen: yes, KMS-managed keys for Dedicated/Private and customer-managed keys for Private.
07:02 Sophie Patel: ok thanks, appreciate the walkthrough.
07:05 Lara Chen: thank you everyone, we'll follow up with the docs and pricing.
07:09 Miguel Ortiz: thanks, bye.

End of transcript.
